parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A particle of mass m and positive charge q travels perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B in a circular path of period T. Starting with the magnetic force, derive B = 2πm/(qT).

answer.text: qvB = mv²/r, and v = 2πr/T. Thus B = mv/(qr) = 2πm/(qT).

evidence.question: 5bii

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Two identical non-relativistic charged particles enter the same uniform magnetic field at right angles. One orbit has twice the radius of the other. Compare their orbital periods and explain your answer.

answer.text: The periods are equal. T = 2πm/(|q|B), independent of radius. The particle in the larger orbit also has proportionally greater speed.

evidence.question: 5biii
evidence.review: Worked answer checked against the source marking guidance; wording adapted for independent IB practice.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A charged particle moves at 1.1 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.052 T. An electric field is added so that the particle continues with constant velocity. Calculate the required electric field strength.

answer.text: The electric and magnetic forces must be equal and opposite: |q|E = |q|vB. E = vB = 5.7 × 10⁴ N C⁻¹.

evidence.question: 5biv
evidence.review: Worked answer checked against the source marking guidance; wording adapted for independent IB practice.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A loose metal helical spring rests on a smooth table with equally spaced turns. Flexible leads connect its ends to a dc supply. Describe and explain how the spacing between turns changes when current starts flowing.

answer.text: The spacing decreases. Adjacent turns carry current in the same sense. Each turn’s magnetic field acts on the current in neighbouring turns, producing attraction.

evidence.question: 6b
evidence.review: Worked answer checked against the source marking guidance; wording adapted for independent IB practice.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Particle 1 has charge −Q and particle 2 has charge +2Q. Each starts from rest and is accelerated through a potential difference of the same magnitude ΔV, with polarity chosen to accelerate that particle. Determine K2/K1.

answer.text: The kinetic energy gained is |q|ΔV. Thus K1 = QΔV, K2 = 2QΔV and K2/K1 = 2.

evidence.question: 4a
evidence.review: Worked answer checked against the source marking guidance; wording adapted for independent IB practice.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A particle of mass M/2 and positive charge 2Q enters a uniform field B0 perpendicular to the field at speed v = 2√(K2/M), where K2 is its kinetic energy. It completes a semicircle before leaving the field. Derive its entry-to-exit separation in terms of M, Q, K2 and B0.

answer.text: The radius is r = mv/(qB0) = [(M/2) × 2√(K2/M)]/(2QB0) = √(MK2)/(2QB0). Entry and exit are separated by a diameter: Δx = √(MK2)/(QB0).

evidence.question: 4bii
evidence.review: Worked answer checked against the source marking guidance; wording adapted for independent IB practice.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A negatively charged particle moves vertically down the page through a magnetic field directed out of the page. An electric field is added so that its path is straight and its speed constant. Determine the direction of the electric field.

answer.text: The magnetic force on the negative charge is to the right. Its electric force must be to the left, so the electric field points to the right.
